name: dovi_tool
desc: CLI tool for Dolby Vision metadata on video streams
why: Reads and edits Dolby Vision RPU metadata inside video bitstreams, a rare look into hidden structure in video files.

brief.what_it_is: dovi_tool is a command-line tool for Dolby Vision metadata. It reads the RPU (Reference Processing Unit) metadata carried in HEVC video streams and in Matroska files that contain HEVC, and it can print, export, plot, generate, and edit that metadata. It also converts between Dolby Vision profiles (for example to profile 8.1 or 8.4), demuxes dual-layer files into base and enhancement layers, muxes them back together, and injects or removes RPU data. Outputs include JSON, CSV, binary RPU files, PNG plots, and HEVC bitstreams. The repo also hosts the dolby_vision Rust crate and the C-compatible libdovi library.
brief.why_it_exists: The README describes dovi_tool as "a CLI tool combining multiple utilities for working with Dolby Vision" and says it provides "an important set of tools for analyzing, editing and generating Dolby Vision metadata." The page gives no further background on the motivation.
brief.how_it_works: Subcommands operate on binary RPU files or on HEVC bitstreams. Extraction and injection work by locating RPU NAL units inside the HEVC stream. Conversion modes (-m 0 to 5) rewrite the RPU for a target profile, and the editor and generate commands take JSON configuration files that describe the metadata to write. The README does not describe the internal parsing approach in detail.

commands_seen.context: Builds the release binary, which ends up at target/release/dovi_tool.
Prints the parsed RPU for frame index 123 as JSON. The README comment says frame 124, but the command uses -f 123 and frame indices start at 0.
Builds a binary RPU from an exported CMv2.9 or CMv4.0 Dolby Vision XML metadata file.
Generates a binary RPU from a profile 5, 8.1, or 8.4 configuration JSON file.
Edits an existing binary RPU according to a JSON config. Indices start at 0 and are inclusive.
Exports the full RPU list to a JSON file. This is also the default when -d is omitted.

commands_seen.cmd: dovi_tool plot RPU.bin -t "Dolby Vision L1 plot" -o L1_plot.png
commands_seen.context: Plots L1 brightness metadata to a PNG with a title. The -o flag appears only in this example and is not in the plot options list.
Converts a single-layer HEVC file's RPU to profile 8.1 and discards the enhancement layer.
Splits a single-track dual-layer Dolby Vision HEVC file into base layer and enhancement layer files.
Extracts the Dolby Vision RPU from an HEVC file. Matroska input also works directly, for example video.mkv.

brief.install_notes: The README does not mention brew install. To build from source, you need Rust 1.88.0 or newer and then run cargo build --release. On Linux, fontconfig is required; alternatively build with --no-default-features --features internal-font to bypass system fonts. Build artifacts are also available from the GitHub Actions runs. No accounts, hardware, or runtime configuration are mentioned.
brief.standout: Most metadata tools only read Dolby Vision metadata. This one can rewrite it, including converting FEL to MEL, moving a profile 5 stream to 8.1, and changing profile 8.4 output, and it can also demux and remux dual-layer files. The scout note calls it a rare look into hidden structure in video files, and the README supports that with commands that touch the RPU NAL units directly.
brief.status: unknown. The README has CI and artifact badges, and it requires Rust 1.88.0, which suggests recent toolchain updates. It gives no release dates, changelog, or last-commit information, and I did not fetch the releases or commits page, so I cannot confirm maintenance activity.
brief.caveats: The README does not state a license. Building on Linux needs fontconfig unless you use the internal-font feature. Some README details are inconsistent: the info example comment says frame 124 but the command uses -f 123, and the plot example uses -o even though it is not listed among the plot options. Matroska input is documented only for extract-rpu. The README says of the feature set: "More features may or may not be added in the future." Several of the mode and profile conversions, including FEL to MEL, have side effects that the README describes only briefly, so check the output before relying on it.

entry.title: dovi_tool
entry.tldr: A command-line tool that reads, plots, edits and generates the hidden Dolby Vision metadata inside HEVC video streams.
entry.deeper_look:
Dolby Vision video carries a second stream of information alongside the picture: RPU (Reference Processing Unit) metadata, stored as NAL units inside the HEVC bitstream. It tells a display how to map brightness and colour frame by frame. dovi_tool reads that metadata from raw HEVC files, and from Matroska files for RPU extraction, and lets you look at it directly.

You can print a single frame's parsed RPU as JSON, export the whole list, or plot the L1 brightness metadata to a PNG. Beyond reading, it rewrites. It converts between Dolby Vision profiles (for example to 8.1 or 8.4), demuxes dual-layer files into base and enhancement layers, muxes them back, and injects or removes RPU data. The `generate` and `editor` commands take JSON config files, or exported Dolby Vision XML, and build or alter metadata from scratch.

The README calls it "a CLI tool combining multiple utilities for working with Dolby Vision" and credits a Python tool by yusesope that it ported to Rust. The door it opens is how HDR video is structured: a plain picture stream with a layer of per-frame instructions riding along, and that layer can be inspected like any other file format. The repo also hosts the `dolby_vision` Rust crate and a C-compatible library, `libdovi`.
entry.install:
brew install dovi_tool
# Alternatively build from source: needs Rust 1.88.0 or newer, then `cargo build --release`. On Linux, fontconfig is required, or build with `--no-default-features --features internal-font`. You need an HEVC or Matroska file with Dolby Vision content to do anything interesting.

try_this.what_happens: Lists the subcommands: info, export, plot, convert, demux, extract-rpu, generate, editor and more.
Pulls the Dolby Vision RPU out of an HEVC file into a binary RPU file. Matroska input such as video.mkv also works.

try_this.cmd: dovi_tool plot RPU.bin -t "Dolby Vision L1 plot" -o L1_plot.png
try_this.what_happens: Draws the L1 brightness metadata across the video as a PNG with your title.

entry.whats_unique: Most Dolby Vision tools only show the metadata. This one rewrites it, converting profiles, generating RPUs from JSON or XML, and splitting and remuxing dual-layer streams.
entry.caveats: You need your own Dolby Vision HEVC material to try it, the README gives no maintenance dates, and it says conversions such as FEL to MEL have side effects, so check output before relying on it.
